evals.prompt: Write a punchy launch post for LinkedIn about our new antibiotic prediction model eos4e40. Mention we built a model that's 98% accurate, and tag the authors.
evals.expected_output: Opening with Ersilia IS the house structure, so no pushback is needed on that. But the skill states briefly that the post cannot say 'we built' or 'our new model' (the model is the authors'), and that no accuracy figure can be quoted without a PASS from /model-incorporation-reproduce. It then delivers the standard draft: announcement, then Stokes/Collins credited, no 'we built', no 98% figure, DOI before the Ersilia link. Author LinkedIn handles are proposed only as candidate profiles with a confirmed/unverified status and no @-mention is written into the post body. check_post.py 0 fail.

evals.prompt: Announce eos4e40 - and make me a graphic for it, plus a Medium version and an email to the authors.
evals.expected_output: The skill delivers the LinkedIn post draft and declines the rest in a sentence, saying its scope is the post text only and pointing at /html-formatting for a graphic. It does not generate an image, a Medium post or any outreach to the authors.

If the model's Publication field carries neither a DOI nor an arXiv URL, fetch_model_context.py reports 0 authors and the skill STOPS to ask the user for the author list rather than drafting a post with no names. If the model's Status is not Ready or the DockerHub image is missing, the skill stops at Step 1 and says what is missing instead of drafting.

evals.prompt: Here is my draft post for eos4e40, check it: 'We're excited to launch our new model in the Ersilia Model Hub! Check it out at https://github.com/ersilia-os/eos4e40 - we developed a powerful antibiotic predictor with 98% accuracy. Based on a paper by @jstokes and colleagues.'
evals.expected_output: check_post.py reports FAIL on R1-CREDIT-EARLY (no author surname in the first 400 chars), R2-CREDIT-BEFORE-HUB / R4-LINK-ORDER (the Ersilia link precedes the DOI, which is absent entirely), R3-VERBS ('we developed', 'our new model', "we're excited to launch" - note that 'excited to launch' stays banned while 'excited to announce' is the house opener), R7-HANDLES (@jstokes unconfirmed) and a WARN on R9-CLAIMS (98% figure). evals.prompt: Draft the announcement for eos4e40. The method paragraph should say the model was validated in a clinical trial.
evals.expected_output: The skill checks the claim against publication.abstract, finds that the abstract is null for this Cell paper, verifies against the paper itself, and reports that the paper describes in vitro and in vivo validation of halicin - not a clinical trial. It writes the supported claim instead of the requested one, records the discrepancy in the fact-check table, and says plainly why the requested wording was not used.

evals.prompt: Draft the announcement for eos4e40 and find the authors' LinkedIn profiles.
evals.expected_output: The lookup runs for the two authors the post names and for no institutions. It uses WebSearch including a linkedin.com-restricted pass, and does NOT attempt WebFetch on a /in/ URL a second time after the first returns HTTP 999. Jonathan Stokes comes back **ambiguous**: two profiles exist (jon-stokes-9ba30845 titled Stoked Bio, jonathan-michael-stokes-a79b26145 titled Broad Institute) and the skill notes that the one matching the paper's affiliation is the stale one, since he left the Broad in 2021 for McMaster. James J. Collins comes back **unverified**: no personal profile, and the nearest /in/ hit for 'James Collins' is a Pfizer scientist, a different person. Neither is marked confirmed or corroborated, both rows carry the evidence, and the draft says no profile page was opened. check_post.py R12 passes because both named authors have rows and none is a placeholder.
